docs.title: ralpher
docs.text:
ralpher runs a coding agent in a loop. Each iteration starts a fresh agent process with the same prompt, streams its JSON output to your terminal as readable progress, and records everything to log files. The loop ends when the agent prints a completion marker, when the iteration budget runs out, or when something goes wrong.

It is a "ralph loop": instead of one long agent session that fills its context window, you run many short ones. State lives in the repository (code, commits, a tasks file), not in the conversation, so every iteration starts with a clean context and reads where the last one left off.

bin/ralpher.sh --iterations 5 --prompts 'Fix one failing test, commit, and exit.
If no test fails, print <promise>COMPLETE</promise> on a line of its own.'

docs.title: What it adds over a shell for loop
docs.text:
• Readable progress. The agent's stream-json output is parsed into streamed text, tool calls and task progress lines, coloured by a theme you control. See Terminal output.
  • A stop the agent cannot fake. With a tasks file, a completion marker is accepted only when every task in the file is done. See Task files and queues.
  • Isolation. With --worktree, the agent works in a git worktree named after the tasks file, and ralpher prints the commands to merge and remove it afterwards. See Worktrees and git.
  • Hooks. Run commands (desktop notifications, chat messages) when a run starts, an iteration ends, a task changes status, or the run ends. See Hooks.
  • Records. Raw stdout and stderr, parsed progress, errors and a JSON state file, per iteration. See Logs and state.
  • Safe stops. An agent that asks for an operator, or loops on a blocked task, ends the run with a suggested next prompt; Ctrl+C twice stops the agent's whole process group. See Stopping a run.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• Installation: clone, uv sync, check claude is on PATH.
  • Getting started: a first loop, then a task queue in a worktree.
  • How ralpher works: the model behind every option.
  • Command line: every option and its default.

The default agent arguments skip permission prompts

ralpher runs claude with --dangerously-skip-permissions by default, because an unattended loop cannot answer prompts. The agent can run any command your user can. Run it in a repository you can restore, on a machine or container you are prepared to have changed, or pass your own --args. See Limits.

docs.title: One run, many iterations
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Pre-run git checks] --> B[Read prompt and tasks file]
    B --> C["start hook"]
    C --> D["Iteration i: render prompt, iteration_start hook"]
    D --> E["Start agent process, parse its stream"]
    E --> F["Agent exits, or is stopped"]
    F --> G["iteration_end hook"]
    G --> H{"Marker seen?"}
    H -- "yes, tasks file says all done" --> K[Stop: complete]
    H -- "yes, tasks not done" --> R[Reject the stop] --> I
    H -- no --> I{"Error, termination, or last iteration?"}
    I -- no --> D
    I -- yes --> L[Stop]
    K --> M["end hook, cleanup commands"]
    L --> N["error hook if error, end hook, next prompt if any"]

A run is one invocation of ralpher.sh. It runs up to --iterations iterations. Each iteration starts one agent process:

<agent> <args...> [--settings {...}] [--worktree <name>] <rendered prompt>

with --agent (default claude) and --args split as a shell would. The prompt is the last argument, so it never passes through a shell. stdin is /dev/null; the agent runs in its own process group, in --cwd if given.

Nothing carries over between iterations except what the agent wrote to disk. That is the point: each iteration starts with an empty context, and the prompt tells the agent where to look (a tasks file, git log, a TODO list).

docs.title: Reading the stream
docs.text:
ralpher expects Claude Code's --output-format stream-json with --include-partial-messages: one JSON object per line. Each line is written raw to the stdout log, then classified:

Line What ralpher does text deltas printed as they stream (content_delta style) tool calls the tool name and its main input, such as the command or file path (tool_use style) a <task> block in text or a tool result a task progress line, and an llm_task_progress hook a text line equal to a stop marker marks the iteration complete a result with is_error: true marks the iteration as an error and stops the agent system messages most are skipped; the rest print their subtype an unknown line type logged to the errors file and listed at the end of the iteration

At the end of each iteration ralpher prints the tools used, and any unknown tools or message types, and records them in the state file.

docs.title: Ending the loop
docs.text:
After each iteration, the loop stops if any of these holds:

  • complete: a line of the agent's output was exactly a stop marker (--stops, default <promise>COMPLETE</promise>), and, with a tasks file, the verified stop agrees;
  • error: the agent reported an error result, exited non-zero without writing any stdout, or an I/O failure on the agent's output reader threads was logged as an error;
  • exception: an exception in the iteration itself ends the loop at once, with exit reason exception during iteration <i> and exit status 1;
  • termination: you pressed Ctrl+C twice, ralpher got SIGTERM, the agent asked for an operator, or ralpher detected a loop on a blocked task. See Stopping a run.

Otherwise it runs the next iteration, up to --iterations. Running out of iterations is not an error: the exit reason is completed all iterations and the exit status is 0. See Exit statuses.

The marker must be a whole line on its own, after stripping whitespace. A marker quoted inside a sentence, or inside the prompt the agent echoes, does not count.

docs.title: The agent's environment
docs.text: The agent starts with the environment ralpher was started with, minus ralpher's own Python: bin/activate.sh puts ralpher's .venv/bin on PATH and its src on PYTHONPATH, and ralpher removes both, and VIRTUAL_ENV when it names that .venv, before starting the agent. So python and pytest in the agent's shell are whatever the project's own setup provides (its bin/activate.sh, a direnv .envrc, or your PATH), never ralpher's packages. Any other virtual environment active when ralpher started is kept.

docs.title: Settings and options
docs.text: Command-line options say what to run. Settings, read from JSON files, say how it looks and what to run around it (hooks, theme). Settings are layered: built-in defaults, then ~/.ralpher/settings.json, then .ralpher/settings.json in the --cwd directory (only when --cwd is given), then --settings-file. See Settings.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: Two runs: a plain loop on a prompt, then a task queue in a worktree, which is how ralpher is mostly used.

docs.title: A plain loop
docs.text:
From the root of a git repository with a clean working tree:

ralpher.sh --iterations 3 --prompts 'Read TODO.md, do the first item, commit, and exit.
If TODO.md has no items, print <promise>COMPLETE</promise> on a line of its own.'

ralpher checks the repository (see Worktrees and git), then runs claude up to three times. Each iteration prints the rendered prompt, then the agent's streamed text and tool calls, then a summary of the tools it used. When a line of the agent's output is exactly <promise>COMPLETE</promise>, the loop stops after that iteration.

Put a longer prompt in a file and pass --prompt PROMPT.md instead of --prompts. The prompt is a Jinja template, rendered afresh for each iteration.

Add logs:

ralpher.sh --iterations 3 --prompt PROMPT.md \
  --logdir ralpher-logs/todo --progress progress.log --stdout stdout.jsonl \
  --stderr stderr.jsonl --errors errors.log --state state.json

See Logs and state for what each file holds.

docs.title: A task queue in a worktree
docs.text:
A task queue is a Markdown tasks file worked through by one prompt, one task per iteration, in a git worktree so your checkout stays untouched.

  1. Write a tasks file at agents/tasks/<spec>/tasks-<n>.md. Each task is a ## Task <n>: <title> heading followed by a **Status:** todo line:

    # Tasks: config loader

## Task 1: Add the Settings dataclass

**Status:** todo

Fields and defaults as in the spec...

## Task 2: Read settings from TOML

**Status:** todo

  2. Commit and push it. With --worktree, Claude Code creates the worktree from origin's default branch unless you have set worktree.baseRef to head, so unpushed work is not in it.

  3. From the repository root, run:

    rrq.sh <spec> <n>

    which is ralpher.sh with ralpher's bundled one-task prompt, 20 iterations, --worktree, --task-file agents/tasks/<spec>/tasks-<n>.md and logs under ralpher-logs/<spec>/tasks-<n>/. See Wrapper scripts.

Each iteration, the agent picks the first eligible task, marks it in-progress, does it, runs the project's checks, marks it done and commits. ralpher prints a line as each task starts and finishes:

task 1: Add the Settings dataclass 1/2 start
task 1: Add the Settings dataclass 1/2 done

When every task is done, the agent prints the completion marker, ralpher confirms against the tasks file in the worktree, and prints the commands to merge the branch and remove the worktree:

Probable cleanup commands...
  cd /home/you/src/config-loader && \
  git merge --no-ff --no-edit worktree-config-loader-tasks-1 && \
  (git worktree unlock config-loader-tasks-1 2>/dev/null || true) && \
  git worktree remove --force config-loader-tasks-1 && \
  git branch -D worktree-config-loader-tasks-1 && \
  git push && \
  (git push origin --delete worktree-config-loader-tasks-1 2>/dev/null || true)

Review the branch before you run them: they merge, delete the worktree and push.

If a task needs a decision from you, the agent reports it and ralpher stops with a suggested prompt for an interactive session, for example unblock task 3 in worktree task file <path>. Answer it there, then rerun rrq.sh; the queue resumes from the tasks file.

docs.text:

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: ralpher is run from a checkout; it is not published as a package.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Tool Why Python 3.14.5 or later ralpher's own code (requires-python in pyproject.toml) uv creates ralpher's virtual environment from the lock file git the pre-run checks and worktrees Claude Code (claude), signed in the default agent

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone git@github.com:bnomis/ralpher.git
cd ralpher
uv sync

uv sync creates .venv with the locked runtime dependencies and the dev group. ralpher never installs into, or runs from, your project's environment.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
bin/ralpher.sh --help

prints every option with its default. Then check that the agent starts:

claude --version

docs.title: Make it easy to call
docs.text:
The wrapper scripts find ralpher through RALPHER_PATH. Set it, and put bin on your PATH, in your shell profile:

export RALPHER_PATH="$HOME/src/ralpher"
export PATH="$RALPHER_PATH/bin:$PATH"

bin/ralpher.sh activates ralpher's .venv and puts its src on PYTHONPATH before starting bin/ralpher.py, so it works from any directory. The agent itself does not inherit that environment; see How ralpher works.

docs.title: Optional: the /rrq command for Claude Code
docs.text:
bin/install-claude.sh

symlinks everything under ralpher's claude/ directory into ~/.claude/, which installs the /rrq and /rro commands. It runs the shared installer, install-in-claude, with uvx at the commit pinned in the script, so it needs uv and SSH access to bnomis/install-in-claude; add --dry-run to see what it would change first. An existing symlink at a destination is replaced; an existing regular file is renamed with a .orig suffix, never overwritten. See Driving ralpher from Claude Code.

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
git -C "$RALPHER_PATH" pull
uv --directory "$RALPHER_PATH" sync

docs.title: Claude Code's output format
docs.text: ralpher parses Claude Code's stream-json output. Another agent works only if it writes the same JSON lines; --agent changes the command, not the parser. When Claude Code adds a message type, ralpher logs the new lines to the errors file and lists them at the end of the iteration, and otherwise carries on: the stop marker and task blocks are still found as long as assistant text keeps its shape.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
The default --args include --dangerously-skip-permissions. An unattended loop has nobody to answer a permission prompt, so without it the agent stalls on the first tool that needs approval. With it, the agent can run any command your user can, and a prompt injected through a file, a dependency or a web page it reads is acted on without asking.

Ways to narrow that:

  • run ralpher in a container or a disposable VM;
  • replace --args with an allow-list: --args '--verbose --include-partial-messages --print --output-format stream-json --allowedTools "Bash(pytest:*)" Edit Read';
  • keep secrets out of the environment ralpher starts with: the agent inherits it.

docs.title: Git
docs.text:
• --worktree relies on Claude Code's own worktree support, and on its branch name, worktree-<name>, to find the tasks file for the verified stop.
  • The pre-run checks prompt on the terminal, so they wait in an unattended run. Commit and push first, or pass --skip-git-check.
  • The pre-run checks do not read a --settings you pass in --args; they take the base ref from --worktree-base-ref or Claude Code's settings files.
  • The cleanup commands are printed for you to run; ralpher never merges, deletes or pushes.

docs.title: The stop marker
docs.text: The agent decides when it is finished. Without --task-file, nothing checks it: a premature marker ends the loop, and a forgotten one runs every iteration. With a tasks file, the verified stop catches the first case, not the second.

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text: Two runs with the same tasks file and --worktree share a worktree, and would edit the same files. Run one queue per tasks file at a time.

docs.title: Platforms
docs.text: ralpher is developed on macOS and Linux. Stopping the agent uses process groups (os.killpg), and the bundled scripts are bash.

docs.title: Running an order of task lists
docs.text:
A large piece of work is often several task lists that must run in a set order. An order file names those lists, says which must be merged before another may start, and holds the settings for a slower whole-project check (a checkpoint) that runs every few lists. /rro runs the whole order from that file: each list is merged before the next starts, and the stops the session decided along the way are gathered into a batch review for you.

The order file is the only state. A new session given the same file carries on where the last one stopped.

docs.title: An example order
docs.text:
Save this as agents/tasks/order-example.md. Text outside the two tables is kept as written.

# Order: example

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| checkpoint command | `make test-slow` |
| checkpoint every | 3 |
| test log | `ralpher-logs/{spec}/tasks-{index}/final-tests.log` |
| test pass line | `all selected test directories passed` |
| test fail pattern | `FAILED` |
| always wait for | `claude/rules/queue-stops.md` |
| progress page | |

| # | Task list | Waits for | Stops for you | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `parser/tasks-1.md` | - | - | todo |
| 2 | `lexicon/tasks-1.md` | - | the verdicts on the new entries (Task 3) | todo |
| | **Checkpoint** | | | todo |
| 3 | `report/tasks-2.md` | 1 | - | todo |
| | **Final checkpoint** | | | todo |

Run it from the main checkout, on the default branch, with a clean tree that is level with its remote:

/rro agents/tasks/order-example.md

agents/tasks/run-order/example-order.md in ralpher's checkout holds the same tables, and the tests read it.

docs.title: The order table
docs.text:
Column Meaning # A label without spaces (3a is allowed). Labels are unique. Task list A path under agents/tasks/, as <spec>/tasks-<index>.md. It must exist. Waits for -, or labels separated by commas. Each must be merged before the row may start. Stops for you Free text naming the stops that always wait for you in that list. - means none beyond the always wait for rule files. Status Written by /rro only: todo, running, waiting: <what>, merged <short hash>, and for a checkpoint passed <counts> or failed <counts>.

A **Checkpoint** row may be written by hand. Where the table has none, /rro runs one after every checkpoint every merged lists and after the last. A **Final checkpoint** row ends the order.

Rows run in table order. A row that waits for an unmerged row is an error, not something to skip: the table order is yours.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
An order file with no settings table, or without a required setting, is an error before anything runs.

Setting Default Trade-off checkpoint command required Run from the main checkout on the default branch, in the background. Use your slowest whole-project test command; the per-list gate covers the rest. checkpoint every 3 Lists merged between checkpoints when the table has no checkpoint rows. A smaller number finds a regression sooner and names fewer suspect lists, at the cost of more slow runs. test log ralpher-logs/{spec}/tasks-{index}/final-tests.log Path, relative to the main checkout, where a list's last task saves its final test output. {spec} and {index} are filled per list. An absolute path, or one containing .., is refused, so the log is always read from inside the repository. test pass line required A line the log must contain for the run to count as passed. Choose one only a complete, successful run prints. test fail pattern FAILED Regular expression; any match in the log fails the gate. always wait for empty Comma-separated rule files whose listed stops are never decided, in addition to /rrq's own exceptions. progress page empty Artifact URL of the progress page. /rro fills it in when it first publishes one.

docs.title: What /rro does
docs.text:
1. Start. Checks it is in the main checkout on the default branch, clean and level with its remote, then asks bin/rro.sh next for the next step. A malformed order file or an unmet Waits for stops here, before anything runs.
  2. A list. Sets the row to running, commits the order file, and runs the list as /rrq --decide <spec> <index> does. The stops /rrq --decide settles carry a Queue-decision: trailer in their commit.
  3. Merge. When every task is done, checks the saved test log, then merges with --no-ff, runs the pre-push hooks, pushes, removes the list's worktree and branch, and sets merged <hash>. It never forces and never skips hooks.
  4. A checkpoint. Runs the checkpoint command in the background, one test run on the machine at a time. On a pass it sets passed <counts>, writes the batch review agents/reviews/queue-decisions-<n>.md from the decisions since the previous checkpoint, publishes its page, and goes on to the next list without waiting for your answers.
  5. Progress page. One page per order, from the template claude/templates/order-progress.html, rebuilt from the order file at every list start, task start and finish, stop, merge and checkpoint. Beside the order's rows and checkpoints it shows the running list: which task of how many is running, how many are done, the time spent so far, and an ETA for the list and for the order from the average minutes per task of the lists already merged.
  6. Finish. After the final checkpoint, reports the merged lists, the checkpoints and the decisions awaiting review.

Without the Artifact tool, /rro writes the review document, says no page was published, and carries on.

docs.title: What stops for you
docs.text:
• A stop named in a row's Stops for you cell or in an always wait for rule file. The row becomes waiting: <the stop>.
  • A failed test gate: a missing log, no pass line, or a fail-pattern match. If the log names failing directories, /rro reruns them serially and merges only if they pass; otherwise the row becomes waiting: test gate.
  • A merge conflict, a rejected push or a failing pre-push hook.
  • A failed checkpoint. The row becomes failed <counts>, and the lists merged since the last passing checkpoint are reported, newest first, as the suspects.

docs.title: The last task saves the test log
docs.text: The merge gate reads the log at the test log path; it does not rerun the tests. So the last task of every list in an order must save its final test output there. The shared task-list skill is meant to do this; until it does, write the path into the last task of each list by hand.

docs.title: Resuming
docs.text:
The order file is the state. After a lost session, run /rro with the same file:

  • a running list: the session checks whether its queue is still running and, if not, runs it again;
  • a waiting: ... row: it asks you about the stop the row names;
  • a failed checkpoint: it tells you and waits.

docs.title: The script
docs.text:
/rro calls bin/rro.sh, which prints one line of JSON per call:

bin/rro.sh next agents/tasks/order-example.md
bin/rro.sh check-log agents/tasks/order-example.md 1
bin/rro.sh set-status agents/tasks/order-example.md 1 running
bin/rro.sh decisions agents/tasks/order-example.md --since <ref>
bin/rro.sh set-setting agents/tasks/order-example.md "progress page" <url>

next returns a label on every checkpoint step and row, and set-status takes it unchanged. An explicit checkpoint row's label is checkpoint:<n>, counting checkpoint rows from 1; an implicit checkpoint's is Checkpoint after <label>, naming the list it follows. set-status refuses a status that contains a line break, and restores the order file if the write leaves one that rro cannot read. set-setting writes one setting's value and refuses a name that is not a known setting.

An expected error prints {"error": "<class>", "message": "..."} and exits 2. The command is installed by bin/install-claude.sh beside /rrq.

docs.title: Driving ralpher from Claude Code
docs.text: A queue takes from minutes to hours. You can start it from an interactive Claude Code session and have that session relay progress, then deal with the result: review the branch, run the cleanup commands, answer an operator stop.

docs.title: The /rrq command
docs.text:
bin/install-claude.sh installs /rrq into ~/.claude/commands/. In a session at a project's root:

/rrq config-loader 1

The session:

  1. runs $RALPHER_PATH/bin/rrq.sh config-loader 1 in the background, from the main checkout even if the session is in a worktree;
  2. watches the output for task progress and loop-end lines, and relays each as one short line: ▶ start, ✓ done, ✗ blocked, ? operator, ■ loop end;
  3. when the queue exits, shows the last 100 lines of its output, which hold the exit reason and either the cleanup commands or the next prompt.

/rrq --decide <spec> <n> lets the session settle an operator stop itself, rather than stopping for you.

/rro <order file> runs several task lists in a set order, merging each and checking in between; see Running an order of task lists.

The command file is claude/commands/rrq.md in ralpher's checkout. Read it before you rely on it; edit it to change what the session relays.

docs.title: Without the command
docs.text: Any program can follow a queue: run rrq.sh with its output going to a file, and filter that file as shown in Terminal output. The state file gives the outcome as JSON once the run ends.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
A hook is a command ralpher starts when something happens in a run: a desktop notification when a queue finishes, a chat message when a task is blocked. Hooks are set in settings under hooks, as a list of commands per event:

{
  "hooks": {
    "end": [
      "terminal-notifier -title '{{cwd_basename}} {{task_file_dir_basename}}' -message '{{exit_reason}} after {{iterations_completed}}/{{iterations}}, {{total_time_readable}}'"
    ],
    "llm_task_progress": [
      "terminal-notifier -title '{{cwd_basename}}' -message 'task {{task_id}} {{task_status}}: {{task_title}}'"
    ]
  }
}

Warning

Hooks run as commands. The .ralpher/settings.json in the --cwd repository can define them, so run ralpher only on repositories you trust.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Event When Extra variables start after the pre-run checks, before the first iteration iteration (0), prompt (unrendered) iteration_start before an iteration's agent starts iteration, prompt (rendered) agent_process_start the agent process has started agent_process_id agent_process_end the agent process has exited, or ralpher has stopped it agent_process_id, agent_exit_code (negative when a signal ended it; None if it was still running after ralpher tried to stop it) llm_task_progress a task progress line: a <task> block, or a task newly marked in-progress task_id, task_title, task_index, task_count, task_status iteration_end after an iteration's agent has exited iteration, iteration_time_readable, iteration_time_seconds error the run ended with an error, before end as end end the run ended, for any reason iteration (0), exit_reason, iterations_completed, total_time_readable, total_time_seconds

Every event also gets the variables in Template variables.

docs.title: How a hook runs
docs.text:
• The command is split into arguments as a POSIX shell would (shlex.split) and started directly, not through a shell: no pipes, redirection or $VAR expansion. For those, call sh -c '...'.
  • A value spliced into an sh -c string becomes shell code. That includes the agent-supplied task_title and prompt, so do not put them inside the quoted string; pass them as separate arguments instead.
  • It starts in its own session, with stdout and stderr discarded, and ralpher does not wait for it. A hook that fails to start is logged and ignored.
  • An event with the same type and the same values runs its hooks once per run, so a task block the agent repeats does not notify twice.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
With hook_templates set to true (the default), each command is a sandboxed Jinja template, rendered with the event's variables.

Values are substituted after the command has been split into arguments, so you never escape them. A value containing quotes, spaces or newlines lands in exactly one argument: a task title such as Give each module's config a name neither breaks the command nor splits it. Quote the template for readability if you like; the quoting applies to the template, not to the values.

Four filters work on paths: basename, dirname, stem and suffix.

{{ task_file | dirname | basename }}   {# config-loader #}
{{ task_file | stem }}                 {# tasks-1 #}

With hook_templates set to false, the command is split and run as written.

docs.title: Icons and sounds
docs.text:
Two settings give notification hooks a shared icon and sound:

Setting Becomes Notes hook_icon {{hook_icon}} a template for a file path; set only if the file exists, otherwise a warning is logged hook_sound {{hook_sound}} a template; a sound name, or a path (a value containing /), which is warned about if missing 
{
  "hook_icon": "{{ralpher_root}}/img/ralpher.jpg",
  "hook_sound": "Glass",
  "hooks": {
    "end": ["alerter --app-icon '{{hook_icon}}' --sound '{{hook_sound}}' --title '{{cwd_basename}}' --message '{{exit_reason}}'"]
  }
}

docs.title: Changing hooks during a run
docs.text: Settings are read once at the start. With --load-settings-on-loop they are read again before each iteration, so an edit to a settings file takes effect from the next iteration.

docs.title: Logs and state
docs.text:
Nothing is written unless you ask for it. Each option names a file; with --logdir DIR, the names are relative to DIR, which is created if missing.

Option Holds Per iteration --stdout FILE the agent's raw stdout, one JSON object per line yes --stderr FILE the agent's raw stderr yes --progress FILE everything ralpher prints, as plain text yes, plus a run file --errors FILE lines ralpher could not parse, and parse exceptions yes --state FILE one JSON document for the whole run no 
ralpher.sh ... --logdir ralpher-logs/config-loader/tasks-1 \
  --stdout stdout.jsonl --stderr stderr.jsonl --progress progress.log \
  --errors errors.log --state state.json

docs.title: File names
docs.text:
Per-iteration files get the iteration number before the extension, padded to the width of --iterations: with --iterations 20, progress.log becomes progress-01.log to progress-20.log. The progress file for the run as a whole, with the start banner, loop times and exit reason, is progress-00.log.

If a file of that name already exists, ralpher adds -1, -2 and so on rather than overwriting it, so rerunning a queue into the same --logdir keeps every earlier run: progress-01.log is the first run's iteration 1, progress-01-1.log the second run's.

The state file is not numbered: a rerun with the same --state adds to the same JSON document.

--quiet stops ralpher printing to the terminal; the progress file is still written.

docs.title: The state file
docs.text:
state.json is rewritten after each change, under a lock file (state.json.lock) beside it.

{
  "agent": "claude",
  "args": "--verbose --include-partial-messages --print ...",
  "prompt": "...",
  "max_iterations": 20,
  "start": "2026-11-01T09:12:03.418772",
  "end": "2026-11-01T10:40:51.009311",
  "exit_reason": "complete",
  "stopping_reason": "",
  "iterations_completed": 7,
  "total_time_readable": "1 hour 28 minutes 47 seconds",
  "total_time_seconds": 5327.59,
  "loop_time_readable": "1 hour 28 minutes 33 seconds",
  "loop_time_seconds": 5313.2,
  "overhead_time_readable": "14 seconds",
  "overhead_time_seconds": 14.39,
  "iterations": {
    "01": {
      "start": "2026-11-01T09:12:05.102934",
      "end": "2026-11-01T09:25:40.551203",
      "iteration_time_readable": "13 minutes 35 seconds",
      "iteration_time_seconds": 815.45,
      "tools_used": ["Bash", "Edit", "Read"],
      "stop_rejected": {"total": 7, "not_done": [5, 6, 7]}
    }
  }
}
Key Meaning exit_reason complete, error or termination, joined with , when several apply; completed all iterations; or exception during iteration <i> stopping_reason why a termination happened, such as Operator input required for task 4; empty otherwise overhead_time_* run time outside the agent processes: checks, hooks, startup iterations.<n>.tools_used tool names the agent called iterations.<n>.unknown_tools tools called with an input ralpher could not summarise iterations.<n>.unknown_ptypes stream line types ralpher did not recognise iterations.<n>.stop_rejected a stop marker the verified stop rejected: task count and the numbers of tasks not done

Times are local, without a timezone.

docs.title: Using the logs
docs.text:
• The stdout log is the agent's own record: replay it with jq to see the full tool inputs and results that the terminal shortens.
  • Search the run's progress file for Exit reason: to see how a run ended.
  • errors-<n>.log is empty in a healthy run; lines there usually mean the agent's output format changed. See Limits.

docs.title: Giving the prompt
docs.text:
Option Use --prompt FILE read the prompt from a file --prompts TEXT give the prompt on the command line

--prompt wins when both are given. ralpher exits with an error if the file is missing or empty, or if neither option gives any text. Leading and trailing whitespace is stripped.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
The prompt is a Jinja template, rendered before every iteration. Every value is a string, except worktree, which is a boolean, and worktree_setup, which is a list.

Variable Value iteration this iteration's number, from 1 iterations --iterations task_file absolute path of --task-file, or empty task_file_relative_path --task-file relative to --cwd when it is inside it, otherwise absolute; empty without a tasks file worktree true with --worktree worktree_name the worktree's name, with --worktree and --task-file; otherwise empty worktree_setup a list of strings: the worktree_setup commands with --worktree, otherwise empty anything from --vars its value

The template renders in Jinja's sandbox, the same one hooks use. A template that reaches for something the sandbox blocks (for example {{ ''.__class__ }}), or has a syntax error, stops the run with an error naming the problem.

You are on iteration {{ iteration }} of {{ iterations }}.
{% if worktree %}
Work only in the worktree {{ worktree_name }}.
{% endif %}
Read {{ task_file_relative_path }} and do the first task whose status is todo.

The bundled one-task.md lists the worktree_setup commands for the agent to run first. A custom prompt can loop over them:

{% for command in worktree_setup %}
Run `{{ command }}` in the worktree before anything else.
{% endfor %}

docs.title: --vars
docs.text:
ralpher.sh --prompt PROMPT.md --vars area=parser --vars max_files=5

Each --vars KEY=VALUE adds a variable; split at the first =, so values can contain =. A value with no =, or a key that names a built-in variable (iteration, iterations, task_file, task_file_relative_path, worktree, worktree_name, worktree_setup), stops the run before the start hook with an error and exit status 1.

docs.title: Writing a prompt for a loop
docs.text:
Each iteration starts with no memory of the last, so a loop prompt:

  • says where the state is: a tasks file, a TODO list, git log;
  • asks for one unit of work, then an exit, so each iteration is short and its context small;
  • says exactly when to print the stop marker, on a line of its own, and when not to: an agent told only "print COMPLETE when done" may print it after its own unit of work;
  • asks the agent to commit, so the next iteration, and you, can see what happened.

docs.title: The bundled one-task prompt
docs.text:
agents/prompts/one-task.md in ralpher's checkout is the prompt rrq.sh uses. Per iteration, it tells the agent to:

  1. check the tasks file's integrity: a done task with unchecked boxes is reopened, and work found in git log but not marked is marked;
  2. print the stop marker if every task is done;
  3. pick the first todo task whose dependencies are done, otherwise the first in-progress one;
  4. stop with an operator task block if the task needs a human;
  5. announce it with a start task block, mark it in-progress, implement it, run every check the project defines (pre-commit, including the pre-push stage, and verification scripts), run the tests;
  6. mark it done, commit with a message starting Task <n>:, print a done task block, and exit.

A task whose tests fail for reasons outside its scope is left in-progress, new tasks are added for the fix, and the agent prints a blocked task block. Copy the prompt and edit it for your own conventions; pass your copy with --prompt.

docs.title: From the keyboard
docs.text:
Action Effect Ctrl+C once a warning: press again within 3 seconds to exit Ctrl+C twice within 3 seconds graceful shutdown SIGTERM graceful shutdown any of these during a shutdown immediate exit, status 1

A graceful shutdown sends SIGTERM to the agent's process group, so the agent's own children (test runners, servers) stop too, retrying up to three times. The current iteration ends, iteration_end and end hooks run, the state file is completed, and ralpher exits with status 1 and exit reason termination.

The agent may have been mid-edit. With --worktree your checkout is untouched; inspect the worktree before rerunning.

docs.title: Stops the agent asks for
docs.text:
Cause Stopping reason Next prompt printed an operator task block Operator input required for task <n> unblock task <n> in [worktree ]task file <path> the same blocked task block a third time Loop detected for task <n> with status blocked the same

Both stop the agent within a few seconds of the block, and end the run as a termination. The next prompt is meant for an interactive agent session in the same repository: it names the task and the tasks file the agent was editing (the worktree copy with --worktree).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
An agent result message flagged is_error (out of usage, an API error) stops the agent and ends the run with exit reason error. The error hook runs, then end.

An agent that exits with a non-zero status before writing anything to stdout, as when it refuses its arguments, also ends the run with exit reason error and status 1: every later iteration would pass the same arguments and fail the same way. ralpher logs The agent exited with code <n> without any output; stopping the loop, and the agent's own message is in the stderr log. An exit after a termination signal does not count.

An exception inside ralpher during an iteration is logged, and ends the run as an error with exit reason exception during iteration <n> and status 1. The error hook runs, then end; iteration_end does not run for that iteration.

docs.title: Ending without stopping
docs.text: A run that uses every iteration without a stop marker exits with status 0 and exit reason completed all iterations. Check the tasks file, or the progress file, to see how far it got; rerun to continue.

docs.title: Task files and queues
docs.text: --task-file PATH tells ralpher which Markdown file holds the queue's tasks. ralpher reads it to name the worktree, to show which task has started, and to check a stop marker. The agent is the only thing that edits it.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
ralpher parses two kinds of line:

## Task 3: Read settings from TOML

**Status:** in-progress
  • a task heading, ## Task <number>: <title>;
  • the first **Status:** <value> line after it, before the next ## heading. The value is lowercased; a task with no status line counts as not done.

Everything else is ignored, including headings and status lines inside fenced code blocks (``` or ~~~), so a tasks file can show an example task without it being counted. Statuses the bundled prompt uses are todo, in-progress and done; ralpher only distinguishes done, and in-progress for start lines.

The file must exist and not be empty when the run starts.

docs.title: Task blocks
docs.text:
The agent reports progress by printing a <task> block in its text output:

<task>
<id>3</id>
<title>Read settings from TOML</title>
<index>3</index>
<count>7</count>
<status>done</status>
</task>

status is one of start, done, blocked or operator. ralpher prints a progress line for each block and fires an llm_task_progress hook:

task 3: Read settings from TOML 3/7 done

ralpher also polls the tasks file every few seconds while the agent runs, and prints a start line for any task newly marked in-progress, because agents often skip the start block. Each task gets one start line per iteration.

Two statuses end the run:

Status What happens operator The task needs a person. The agent is stopped and the run ends as a termination, printing Probable next prompt... and unblock task <n> in [worktree ]task file <path>. blocked, the identical block a third time in one run Looks like a loop. The run ends as a termination with the same next prompt.

docs.title: Verified stop
docs.text:
With --task-file, a stop marker is checked against the tasks file before the loop stops:

  • The check passes when every task's status is done.
  • With --worktree, ralpher reads the copy of the tasks file inside the agent's worktree (the worktree whose branch is worktree-<name>), never the copy in your checkout.
  • On rejection ralpher prints ===== Loop complete signal rejected, <n> of <m> tasks not done =====, lists the unfinished tasks, records stop_rejected for the iteration in the state file, and runs the next iteration. A rejection on the last iteration ends the run with completed all iterations.
  • If the check cannot be made (file missing or unreadable, no tasks found, worktree not found), ralpher logs a warning, trusts the marker and stops.

--no-verify-stop skips the check and stops on any marker. Use it when the tasks file does not follow the format above. The cost is that one premature marker ends the whole queue.

Without --task-file the check never runs.

docs.title: Running a queue
docs.text:
rrq.sh <spec> <n> runs agents/tasks/<spec>/tasks-<n>.md with the bundled one-task prompt in a worktree. The equivalent call:

ralpher.sh --cwd "$PWD" --worktree \
  --task-file agents/tasks/<spec>/tasks-<n>.md \
  --prompt "$RALPHER_PATH/agents/prompts/one-task.md" \
  --iterations 20 \
  --logdir ralpher-logs/<spec>/tasks-<n> \
  --stdout stdout.jsonl --stderr stderr.jsonl --progress progress.log \
  --errors errors.log --state state.json

Rerunning the same command after a stop resumes the queue: the worktree is reused, and the agent reads the tasks file to find where it is. Each run writes new log files beside the old ones; see Logs and state.

Set --iterations above the number of tasks. Some iterations do no task work: one that only repairs the tasks file, one that finds a task blocked.

docs.title: What a run prints
docs.text:
1. A banner: start time, agent, arguments, the unrendered prompt, iterations.
  2. For each iteration: the rendered prompt; then, as the agent works, its streamed text, each tool call with its main input, and task progress lines; then the tools used; then the end time and duration.
  3. At the end: each iteration's duration, the total time, the loop time and overhead when the overhead is a second or more, the exit reason, and either the cleanup commands or a suggested next prompt.

Agent stderr is printed in the error style as it arrives.

docs.title: Lines worth watching for
docs.text:
Line Meaning task 3: Read settings from TOML 3/7 start a task started (done, blocked, operator likewise) ===== Loop complete signal received, stopping after 7 iterations. ===== the run is ending; the word is the exit reason ===== Loop complete signal rejected, 3 of 7 tasks not done ===== a stop marker failed the verified stop Probable cleanup commands... see After the queue Probable next prompt... the run stopped for you; paste the prompt into an interactive session

To follow a queue from another program, filter the progress file, or ralpher's stdout, with grep -E '^task [0-9]+|^=+ Loop .* signal (received|rejected)'.

docs.title: Themes
docs.text:
Each line is printed in a style chosen by its kind. Set the styles under theme in settings, as Rich style strings:

{
  "theme": {
    "alert": "bold red",
    "content_delta": "cyan",
    "default": "grey30",
    "error": "red",
    "progress": "yellow",
    "regular": "grey30",
    "system": "yellow",
    "tool_use": "magenta"
  }
}

These are the defaults.

Key Used for alert signal handling: Ctrl+C, shutdown, the pre-run prompts content_delta the agent's streamed text error agent stderr, error results, the loop-end line after an error progress task progress lines regular ralpher's own messages: banners, prompts, times system ralpher and agent system messages, such as Started agent process; the loop-end and rejection lines tool_use tool calls default any kind with no key of its own

A theme in a settings file replaces the whole default theme, not single keys, so give every key you care about; the rest fall back to default, then to grey30. See how settings are merged.

docs.title: Pre-run checks
docs.text:
Before the first iteration, ralpher checks the repository that contains --cwd (or the current directory), and asks before carrying on:

Check Prompt default Not in a git repository continue? no Working tree has changes, including untracked files continue? no The current branch has commits its upstream lacks (after git fetch origin) continue? no ralpher cannot tell whether there are unpushed commits (no origin, a failed fetch, a detached HEAD or no upstream) continue? no With --worktree and a fresh base: origin/HEAD is not the current branch exit now? yes

The unpushed-commits check is skipped when worktrees are created from the local HEAD (below). When ralpher cannot tell whether there are unpushed commits, it says so and asks whether to continue; the default is no, and answering no exits.

The prompts read from the terminal, so an unattended run that hits one waits. Commit and push first, or pass --skip-git-check to skip every check.

docs.title: --worktree
docs.text:
With --worktree, ralpher adds --worktree <name> to the agent's arguments, and Claude Code runs the agent in a git worktree of that name, on the branch worktree-<name>. Every iteration passes the same name, so every iteration uses the same worktree. --args may not contain --worktree or -w: ralpher refuses it with an error, so every check and hook agrees with the agent on whether a worktree is used.

The name comes from the tasks file's absolute path: its directory name and its stem, joined with -, lowercased, with every run of characters other than a-z and 0-9 turned into one -. Claude Code accepts worktree names of at most 64 characters, so a longer name is cut to at most 55 characters and ends with - and the first 8 hex digits of the full name's SHA-256; the branch is still worktree-<name>.

--task-file Worktree Branch agents/tasks/config-loader/tasks-1.md config-loader-tasks-1 worktree-config-loader-tasks-1 TASKS.md <repo-dir>-tasks worktree-<repo-dir>-tasks

Without --task-file, --worktree is passed on its own and Claude Code picks the name.

The prompt must tell the agent to work in the worktree; the bundled one-task prompt does when {{ worktree }} is true. See Prompts.

docs.title: Giving the worktree an environment
docs.text:
The agent creates the worktree empty: it has no virtual environment and no installed hooks. A check that falls back to the tool on PATH then runs a different version from the one the project pins. Set worktree_setup in .ralpher/settings.json to a list of commands:

{
  "worktree_setup": ["uv sync"]
}

With --worktree, the bundled one-task.md prompt tells the agent to run each command in the worktree, in order, before anything else, and to report the task blocked if one fails, rather than borrow another checkout's environment. Every iteration's agent runs the commands, so each must be safe to repeat.

Without the setting, ralpher prints a warning before the first iteration and carries on. See Settings.

docs.title: Where the worktree starts
docs.text:
Claude Code's worktree.baseRef setting decides what a new worktree is created from:

  • fresh (Claude Code's default): origin's default branch. Unpushed commits and local changes are not in the worktree.
  • head: your local HEAD, without uncommitted changes.

--worktree-base-ref fresh|head passes the setting to the agent as --settings '{"worktree": {"baseRef": "..."}}'. --args may not contain --settings: ralpher refuses it with an error. See the Claude Code settings reference.

The pre-run checks use the same value the agent gets: --worktree-base-ref when ralpher passes it, otherwise worktree.baseRef from Claude Code's settings files (user, project, local and managed).

docs.title: Flags refused in --args
docs.text:
--args holds Use instead --worktree or -w ralpher's --worktree --settings --worktree-base-ref, or ralpher's settings files

ralpher stops before the first iteration with an Error: line naming the flag. The tasks file ralpher reads for the stop check and for hook prompts is the worktree copy only under --worktree.

docs.title: After the queue
docs.text:
When a run ends complete, with no error or termination, and used --worktree and --task-file, ralpher prints the commands to fold the work back in:

Probable cleanup commands...
  cd <repository root> && \
  git merge --no-ff --no-edit worktree-<name> && \
  (git worktree unlock <name> 2>/dev/null || true) && \
  git worktree remove --force <name> && \
  git branch -D worktree-<name> && \
  git push && \
  (git push origin --delete worktree-<name> 2>/dev/null || true)

The cd line appears when --cwd is set, as rrq.sh sets it. They are printed, never run. Run them from your checkout of the branch the worktree started from. git branch -D is used rather than -d because a branch pushed for CI, then committed to, is refused by -d even once merged, and the chain would stop before the push.

--cleanup prints the same commands without running anything, for a queue that finished earlier:

ralpher.sh --cleanup --worktree --task-file agents/tasks/config-loader/tasks-1.md

rcl.sh <spec> <n> is that call for a queue started with rrq.sh.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
ralpher.sh [OPTIONS]

bin/ralpher.sh --help prints the same list from the code.

docs.title: What to run
docs.text: Option Default Description --agent AGENT claude The agent command. --args ARGS --verbose --include-partial-messages --print --dangerously-skip-permissions --output-format stream-json The agent's arguments, split as a shell would. Replaces the default entirely. --worktree, -w and --settings are refused; see Worktrees. --prompt FILE Read the prompt from a file. --prompts TEXT The prompt as text. Ignored when --prompt is given. --iterations N 3 The most iterations to run; at least 1. --cwd DIR the current directory The directory the agent runs in, and the git checks run in. Also adds DIR/.ralpher/settings.json to the settings files. --vars KEY=VALUE A prompt template variable. Repeatable. See Prompts.

docs.title: Tasks and stopping
docs.text: Option Default Description --task-file FILE The tasks file. Names the worktree, and turns on the verified stop. Must exist and not be empty. --stops MARKER <promise>COMPLETE</promise> A completion marker: a line of agent output equal to it ends the loop. Repeatable; giving it replaces the default. --no-verify-stop off Trust a marker without checking the tasks file.

docs.title: Worktrees and git
docs.text: Option Default Description --worktree off Pass --worktree <name> to the agent, the name taken from the tasks file. See Worktrees and git. --worktree-base-ref fresh\|head Pass Claude Code's worktree.baseRef setting with --settings. --skip-git-check off Skip the pre-run checks. --cleanup off Print the worktree cleanup commands for --worktree and --task-file, and exit without running anything.

docs.title: Output and logs
docs.text:
Option Default Description --logdir DIR Directory for the files below. Created if missing. --stdout FILE Raw agent stdout, per iteration. --stderr FILE Raw agent stderr, per iteration. --progress FILE Everything printed, per iteration, plus a run file. --errors FILE Unparsed lines and parse errors, per iteration. --state FILE The run's JSON state file. With --logdir, it must be a relative path without ... --quiet off Print nothing to the terminal. Log files are still written.

See Logs and state.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Option Default Description --settings-file FILE A settings file read after the others, so its keys win. --load-settings-on-loop off Read the settings files again before each iteration.

See Settings.

docs.title: Other
docs.text:
Option Description -h, --help Show the options and exit. --completion generate Print shell completion source.

Options take their value either as --iterations 5 or --iterations=5.

docs.title: Exit statuses
docs.text:
Status When Exit reason 0 the agent printed a stop marker that passed the verified stop complete 0 every iteration ran without a stop completed all iterations 0 --help, --cleanup 1 the agent reported an error result error 1 the agent exited non-zero without writing any stdout, as when it refuses its arguments error 1 an exception inside ralpher during an iteration exception during iteration <n> 1 Ctrl+C twice, SIGTERM, an operator task block, or a loop on a blocked task termination 1 a signal during shutdown none: ralpher exits at once 1 a ralpher error before the first iteration: an unreadable or invalid settings file, an invalid --args, a --cwd that cannot be entered, a log directory that cannot be created, a --state path outside the log directory none: ralpher prints Error: ... 1 a pre-run check you answered "no" to (for the divergence check, "yes"), a missing or empty prompt or tasks file, an invalid --vars none: ralpher stops before the first iteration and prints why

When several apply in one iteration, the exit reason joins them, such as complete, termination, and the status is 1 if any is error or termination.

The exit reason is printed as Exit reason: at the end of the run, stored in the state file, and given to the end and error hooks as {{exit_reason}}. A termination also prints Stopping reason: with its cause.

docs.title: Wrapper scripts
docs.text: All live in ralpher's bin/. Each shell wrapper activates ralpher's .venv first (install-claude.sh runs the shared installer with uvx and does not). ralpherun.sh, rrq.sh and rcl.sh need RALPHER_PATH set to ralpher's checkout.

docs.title: ralpher.sh
docs.text:
ralpher.sh [OPTIONS]

ralpher itself; every option is passed through.

docs.title: rrq.sh
docs.text:
rrq.sh SPEC INDEX

Runs a task queue. From your project's root:

Passed to ralpher Value --cwd the current directory --task-file agents/tasks/SPEC/tasks-INDEX.md --prompt ralpher's agents/prompts/one-task.md --iterations 20 --worktree on --logdir ralpher-logs/SPEC/tasks-INDEX --stdout, --stderr, --progress, --errors, --state stdout.jsonl, stderr.jsonl, progress.log, errors.log, state.json

SPEC and INDEX must not contain / or ..; rrq.sh and rcl.sh print a usage message and exit otherwise.

Add ralpher-logs/ to your project's .gitignore.

docs.title: rcl.sh
docs.text:
rcl.sh SPEC INDEX

Prints the cleanup commands for the queue rrq.sh SPEC INDEX ran, and exits. Runs nothing.

docs.title: ralpherun.sh
docs.text:
ralpherun.sh ITERATIONS PROMPT LOGDIR [TASKS]

Runs ralpher with --worktree, the five log files in LOGDIR, and --task-file TASKS when given. Its --cwd is the directory above the script's bin/, which is ralpher's own checkout, so it is for running loops on ralpher itself. For another project, use rrq.sh or ralpher.sh --cwd.

docs.title: install-claude.sh
docs.text:
bin/install-claude.sh [--dry-run] [any other install-in-claude option]

Symlinks the files under ralpher's claude/ into ~/.claude/ by running the shared installer install-in-claude at the commit pinned in the script's INSTALL_IN_CLAUDE_REV, with --source claude and no settings edits. Extra arguments pass through. To upgrade the installer, set INSTALL_IN_CLAUDE_REV to a newer commit and run bin/install-claude.sh --dry-run first. See Driving ralpher from Claude Code.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Settings are JSON objects read from files. None is required.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
Read in this order; a later file's keys win:

  1. built-in defaults (the theme only);
  2. ~/.ralpher/settings.json;
  3. .ralpher/settings.json in the --cwd directory, only when --cwd is given (the wrapper scripts give it);
  4. --settings-file FILE.

The .ralpher/settings.json in the --cwd repository can define hooks, which run as commands, so run ralpher only on repositories you trust.

A file that does not exist is skipped. A file that is not valid JSON stops the run.

Settings are read once, before the first iteration, or before every iteration with --load-settings-on-loop.

docs.title: How files are merged
docs.text: Each file's top-level keys replace the same keys from earlier files; nested objects are not merged. A project file with a hooks object replaces your user file's hooks entirely, and a theme with one key replaces the whole default theme.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Key Type Default Description hooks object: event name to list of command strings none Commands to run on events. See Hooks. hook_templates boolean (true or false, not a string) true Render hook commands as Jinja templates. hook_icon string (template) none A file path offered to hooks as {{hook_icon}}. hook_sound string (template) none A sound name or path offered to hooks as {{hook_sound}}. worktree_setup list of strings none Commands the agent runs in the worktree before anything else, with --worktree. Each must be safe to repeat. See Giving the worktree an environment. theme object: message kind to Rich style see Themes Terminal colours and styles.

Unknown keys are ignored.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
~/.ralpher/settings.json, for macOS notifications with alerter:

{
  "hook_icon": "{{ralpher_root}}/img/ralpher.jpg",
  "hooks": {
    "start": [
      "alerter --app-icon '{{hook_icon}}' --title '{{cwd_basename}} {{task_file_dir_basename}} start' --message 'max iterations {{iterations}}'"
    ],
    "end": [
      "alerter --app-icon '{{hook_icon}}' --title '{{cwd_basename}} {{task_file_dir_basename}} done' --message '{{exit_reason}} {{iterations_completed}}/{{iterations}} {{total_time_readable}}' --sound Funky"
    ],
    "error": [
      "alerter --app-icon '{{hook_icon}}' --title '{{cwd_basename}} {{task_file_dir_basename}} error' --message '{{exit_reason}}' --sound Funky"
    ]
  },
  "theme": {
    "alert": "bold red",
    "content_delta": "cyan",
    "default": "grey30",
    "error": "red",
    "progress": "bold yellow",
    "regular": "grey30",
    "system": "yellow",
    "tool_use": "magenta"
  }
}

docs.title: Template variables
docs.text: Prompts and hook commands are Jinja templates with different variables.

docs.title: Prompts
docs.text:
Rendered before each iteration. See Prompts.

Variable Value iteration this iteration's number, from 1 iterations --iterations task_file absolute path of the tasks file; empty without one task_file_relative_path the tasks file relative to --cwd when inside it, else absolute; empty without one worktree boolean: --worktree given worktree_name the worktree name, with --worktree and --task-file; else empty worktree_setup list of strings: the worktree_setup setting's commands with --worktree, else an empty list each --vars key its value; a key that names a built-in is rejected

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: Rendered when the hook runs, in a sandbox. Values are strings. See Hooks.

docs.title: Every event
